newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopians bury their would-be emperor.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopians bury their would-be emperor.

text.p: Ethiopia's one-time Crown Prince, whose father Emperor Haile Selassie was murdered in 1975, was buried on Sunday in an elaborate ceremony where impoverished aristocrats rubbed shoulders with Rastafarians.

Asfaw Wossen, who in 1988 crowned himself in exile Emperor of Ethiopia -- Ethiopia's 226th emperor in a line extending 3,000 years from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba -- died in the United States on January 17 after a long illness.
He left Ethiopia in 1973 for medical treatment in London and never returned after his father was ousted in a 1974 Marxist coup and murdered by the Marxists the following year.

The body of the 80-year-old was flown to Ethiopia on Saturday night and family members held an all-night vigil before the self-declared emperor was carried to the royal tomb in Addis Ababa's Orthodox Trinity Cathedral.
Thousands of royal supporters and friends, including impoverished elderly aristocrats leaning on walking canes, attended the requiem mass held by Orthodox priests in richly embroidered cloaks.

The coffin was covered in the Royal Standard -- the Ethiopian tricolour carrying the royal coat-of-arms -- the first time the Royal Standard had been displayed in Addis Ababa since the monarchy was overthrown.

When the Marxist government was overthrown in 1991, Asfaw Wossen said he wanted to return to Ethiopia as a constitutional monarch. But government officials have repeatedly said they will not restore the monarchy.
The government did not send an official representative to the funeral.

Asfaw Wossen's wife, Princess Medferiash-Work Abebe, his son Zera-Yacob and other members of the royal family from abroad attended the ceremony, along with members of the Rastafarian sect, who believe Asfaw Wossen's father was the son of God.
The ceremony, attended by thousands of mourners, revived memories of a privileged life in a now vanished era.
Sweeping nationalisation under Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam reduced many of the aristocrats to penury.
The remains of Emperor Haile Selassie, exhumed from under a toilet in the grounds of the imperial palace in 1990, rest in a royal mausoleum in Addis Ababa with other former rulers.
Asfaw Wossen is survived by his wife, four children and many grandchildren. His death has created speculation about the possible declaration of a new successor to the throne, royalists said.
